report:
Scoped PASS for restricted A–E. Original S04 completion remains false: neither universal original question is resolved. The historical full-original INCONCLUSIVE report and the cold result’s candidate=false remain unchanged. I independently checked the complete manuscript, exact-application note, and every mathematical proof in n1–n7, without inheriting their assessments.

The complete support graph is n1=[]; n2=[n1]; n3=[n1,n2]; n4=[n2]; n5=[n1,n2,n3,n4]; n6=[n1,n2,n3,n5]; n7=[n1,n2,n3,n4,n5,n6]. Its seven nodes and eighteen edges are acyclic, and every application establishes its supporting implication’s antecedents. Private histories, protected outputs and artifact paths were not inspected. The worker’s printed constant diagnostic, private symbolic checks and any publisher-erratum claim are outside this certification.

All indispensable primary statements were opened and matched. Bedford–Taylor was accessible through Bedford’s author-hosted copy; Demailly’s PDF is the specified 21 June 2012 version. The previous retrieval limitations therefore do not remain unresolved checks here. Clipped existence, scalar/maximal-coefficient identification, the full test formula and the root-tail characterization are task-granted background, excluded from external premises. Passages indexed -1 document that background. KN Theorem 0.1 was additionally checked: nonzero bounded nonnegative clips are admissible, including clips with zeros.

Operator conversion is exact. Source operator 2D on background 2θ with unchanged potentials preserves the admissible family and multiplies products, capacities and the integration inequality by 2^n. The source density g dV/θ^n leaves the normalization scalar unchanged. Power constants become 2^(-nα)A_0, with the corresponding capacity scaling cancelling in the lower estimate. Bedford–Taylor degree-k closed products scale by (4π)^(-k). No closedness, BMP, positive lower mass or globally smooth exact-background regularization is inserted.

The cold engine n2 retains both torsion contributions. For H=θ+Da, G=θ+Db≥εθ and A_j=∫_V H^j∧G^(n-j), the bounded integration lemma gives A_j≤A_(j+1)+r(A_j+A_(j-1)+A_(j-2)), r=n²Bsε^(-3). The derivative coefficients total at most (n-1)+(n-1)(n-2)≤n²; θ² and θ³ are controlled using G≥εθ. Negative indices are absent. When r≤1/16, induction gives (1-7r)A_j≤A_(j+1), hence A_0≤(1-7r)^(-n)A_n≤2^n A_n. The sharp factor tends to one with s.

For every genuine bounded capacity competitor 0≤w≤1, b=(1-ε)v+tw+m+s leaves reserve (ε-t)θ and dominates t(θ+Dw). The restriction s+t≤ε³/(128n²B) permits comparison with reserve ε/2. The inclusions E_s⊂{a<b}⊂E_(s+t) yield t^n cap(E_s)≤2^n μ(E_(s+t)), over the entire competitor family. The actual a,v are continuous, making positive-level E_s nonempty and open. The backward halving iteration either exhausts the level or halves cap(E_s)^(1/n); an infinite iteration leaving positive level would contradict the w=0 competitor. Its geometric sum proves the lower capacity estimate, including cap(E_s)=cap(X).

The author’s H(x)=A_0^(-1)x^(nα) is admissible, and both κ terms give C_α A_0^(1/n)cap^(α/n), including small A_0. Harmless wording clarification: explicitly include the finite total-capacity endpoint in the manuscript’s power specialization. The supplied supporting recurrence already proves that endpoint; no replacement proof is required.

A and n3 are correct. Fixed legal increments with v=0 and ε=1/2 give s^n≤C A c_j^(1+α)m_j^α. The granted decreasing scalar limit produces exactly b_h(g)≥C m^(-α/(1+α)) for every nonzero measurable g≤f. The cold constant C_A=(s*)^n/[L H_α^(n/(1+α))A^(1/(1+α))] also checks, with L=2^n, H_α=2/(1-2^(-α)), s*=η(1/2)/4. It depends only on X,h,A,α. The granted threshold identity controls the full original rho supremum. Applying it to density tails proves both rho and L^n tail convergence, with zero tails handled by the zero-root convention.

Both proofs of C check. In the manuscript, fixed legal parameters for a proposed gap d give the stated inclusion in {a-v<-d/2}; the directed weighted error contradicts the lower near-minimum capacity. Swapping indices supplies the opposite direction. Independently, n4 takes ε=s/4 and t=s³/(32768n²B), where s=sup(v-a)∈(0,1]. On E_(2t), v-a≥s/2. The recurrence yields I≥c s^(1+3n(1+1/α)), giving the claimed modulus exponent. All competitor reserves and torsion intervals remain legal. Equal measures alone do not establish the weighted hypothesis or homogeneous uniqueness.

For B, clipped measures have one capacity bound and satisfy μ_j≤c_1 f dV. The manuscript’s positive near-minimum capacity and weighted CLN bound cap{φ_j<-L}≤C/L establish bounded oscillation. Independently, n5 uses positive near-minimum mass, normalized L^1 bounds and absolute continuity of the fixed f-integral to exclude depths tending to infinity. Corrected local psh compactness gives a global L^1 subsequence; n2’s Newtonian/harmonic decomposition independently justifies that compactness. The bounded range and fixed finite absolutely continuous f dV give two-index weighted convergence. No higher L^p clip bound is used.

Scaling θ=h/M, u_j=φ_j/M is valid: M^(-n)cap_h≤cap_θ≤cap_h, and the domination constant becomes c_1 A M^(nα). C makes the subsequence uniformly Cauchy. With fixed local closed β=Dq≥h, closed corrected products telescope as D[(φ_j-φ)Σ S_j^a∧S^(k-1-a)]. Smooth testing and uniform mixed-mass bounds control their differences by the uniform potential error. All smooth nonclosed factors (h-β)^(n-k), including their derivatives in testing, remain present. This establishes convergence to the actual Hermitian product. Separately c_j min(f,j)→b_h(f)f in L^1, proving the exact bounded continuous equation and actual mass b_h(f)∫f dV∈(0,∞). The bounded and extended products agree. Only subsequence existence is asserted.

D and n6 check for every given h. The cutoff annulus has a fixed negative-Hessian bound, permitting one small δ with h+Du≥h/2. For β=D|z|², β^n=(n!/π^n)dλ and β^n(B_r)=r^(2n). The tangential and radial eigenvalues are αt^(-1)(1-log t)^(-α-1) and α(α+1)t^(-1)(1-log t)^(-α-2). Their determinant gives the requested pure-top density exactly. The mixed radial flux t^n[Q'(t)]^k gives ball mass r^(2(n-k))α^k(1-log r²)^(-k(α+1)); k=n with δ^n gives exactly the requested pure-top ball formula.

Both no-atom routes are valid. The manuscript dominates every correction term by positive mixed measures and then by a bounded normalized local psh top product; the pluripolar point has zero local capacity. Independently, n6’s smooth Q_ε have positive radial eigenvalue [εq'+tq'']/(t+ε)² and converge uniformly. Uniform annular bounds allow the same δ globally. Actual product passage and the correctly oriented open-ball Portmanteau inequality bound every limiting mixed ball mass by a flux tending to zero at the origin. Smoothness elsewhere proves global absolute continuity, including lower mixed terms and the cutoff.

Lower mixed densities have the stated bounds and O(r²) masses; each degree k<n has some higher L^p integrability. The pure top term is integrable but its p-th power diverges for every p>1. Strict h/2 positivity gives f≥c>0. The pure-top formula excludes the positive lower terms and is not total Hermitian ball mass. The logarithmic potential difference divided by any positive power of R diverges, proving the non-Hölder assertion.

Both all-Borel domination routes work: the manuscript’s exponential radius split and the notes’ radial rearrangement followed by exponential volume-capacity control. Lower mixed terms are controlled separately. Capacity-zero sets have zero smooth volume and zero datum mass by the already proved absolute continuity; finite mass handles larger capacities. DK’s antecedent is applied only to a smooth volume density, and inner regularity extends compact estimates to Borel sets.

Calibration b_h(f)=1 follows from the genuine explicit subsolution and B’s bounded critical solution. If b>1, choose ε with (1-ε)^n b>1. Positive multilinearity supplies the lower product bound, while bounded comparison has a factor tending to one on nonempty open sublevels. Their f-integrals are positive because f≥c, giving a contradiction. No potential uniqueness is inferred. The inclusion {f>K}⊂B_(K^(-1/(4n))) up to a null set gives tail mass O((log K)^(-n(α+1))); A then gives exactly rho-tail rate O((log K)^(-α)).

E and n7 faithfully retain the original problem and criteria. The additional domination assumption is not derived from positive threshold or uniform root tails. The datum has good tails and supplies neither a bad-tail counterexample nor a zero-lower-mass geometry, while applying to any given h with that condition. Historical capacity existence and bounded-range stability are correctly attributed, without priority certification. No essential gap remains in restricted A–E; both original universal questions remain unresolved by this argument.

passages.statement: On a connected compact Hermitian (X,ω), with D_s=i∂bar∂/π, bounded genuine ω-psh a,b,v_1,…,v_(n-1), and T=∧_(i=1)^(n-1)(ω+D_s v_i), satisfy ∫_{a<b}D_s b∧T≤∫_{a<b}D_s a∧T+∫_{a<b}(b-a)D_sT. Kołodziej–Nguyen, arXiv:1312.5491v2, Lemma 2.1.

For a smooth positive Hermitian ω on Ω⊂C^n, 1≤k≤n, and locally bounded genuine ω-psh v_i, the ordinary mixed products ∧_i(ω+D_s v_i), D_s=i∂bar∂/π, converge weakly when each bounded ω-psh sequence decreases pointwise or converges uniformly to v_i. This also holds on compact Hermitian manifolds. Kołodziej–Nguyen, Proposition 1.2.

On compact Hermitian (X,ω), use D_s=i∂bar∂/π and d_s^c=i(bar∂-∂)/(2π). Suppose B>0 satisfies -Bω²≤2nD_sω≤Bω² and -Bω³≤4n²dω∧d_s^cω≤Bω³. For bounded genuine ω-psh a,v, 0<ε<1, m=inf_X[a-(1-ε)v], and U_s={a<(1-ε)v+m+s}, one has ∫_{U_s}(ω+D_s((1-ε)v))^n≤(1+C_nBs/ε^n)∫_{U_s}(ω+D_s a)^n whenever 0<s<ε³/(16B). Kołodziej–Nguyen, Theorem 2.3.

On compact Hermitian (X,ω), with D_s=i∂bar∂/π, cap_ω(E)=sup_{w∈PSH(ω),0≤w≤1}∫_E(ω+D_s w)^n, and B satisfying the torsion bounds -Bω²≤2nD_sω≤Bω² and -Bω³≤4n²dω∧d_s^cω≤Bω³, let bounded genuine ω-psh a≤0 and -1≤v≤0 be given. Set m=inf[a-(1-ε)v], U_s={a<(1-ε)v+m+s}, δ=(1/3)min{ε^n,ε³/(16B)}, δ_0=min{δ,4(1-ε)δ}, 0<ε<1. If H:(0,∞)→(0,∞) is increasing, ∫_1^∞dx/[xH(x)^(1/n)]<∞, and MA_ω(a)(E)≤cap_ω(E)/H(cap_ω(E)^(-1/n)) for every Borel E, then 0<s<δ_0 and 0<cap_ω(U_s)<cap_ω(X) imply s≤κ(cap_ω(U_s)), where κ(y)=4C_n[H(y^(-1/n))^(-1/n)+∫_{y^(-1/n)}^∞dx/(xH(x)^(1/n))]. Independently, 0<s,t≤δ imply [(1-ε)t]^n cap_ω(U_s)≤(1+C_n)MA_ω(a)(U_(s+4(1-ε)t)). Kołodziej–Nguyen, Theorem 5.3 and Lemma 5.4.

On compact Hermitian (X,ω), with D_s=i∂bar∂/π, cap_ω(E)=sup_{w∈PSH(ω),0≤w≤1}∫_E(ω+D_s w)^n, and B satisfying the torsion bounds -Bω²≤2nD_sω≤Bω² and -Bω³≤4n²dω∧d_s^cω≤Bω³, let bounded genuine ω-psh a≤0 and -1≤v≤0 be given. Set m=inf[a-(1-ε)v], U_s={a<(1-ε)v+m+s}, δ=(1/3)min{ε^n,ε³/(16B)}, δ_0=min{δ,4(1-ε)δ}, 0<ε<1. If H:(0,∞)→(0,∞) is increasing, ∫_1^∞dx/[xH(x)^(1/n)]<∞, and MA_ω(a)(E)≤cap_ω(E)/H(cap_ω(E)^(-1/n)) for every Borel E, then 0<s<δ_0 and 0<cap_ω(U_s)<cap_ω(X) imply s≤κ(cap_ω(U_s)), where κ(y)=4C_n[H(y^(-1/n))^(-1/n)+∫_{y^(-1/n)}^∞dx/(xH(x)^(1/n))]. Independently, 0<s,t≤δ imply [(1-ε)t]^n cap_ω(U_s)≤(1+C_n)MA_ω(a)(U_(s+4(1-ε)t)). Kołodziej–Nguyen, Theorem 5.3 and Lemma 5.4.
On connected compact Hermitian (X,ω), genuine ω-psh a,w with sup_X a=0 and 0≤w≤1 satisfy ∫_X|a|(ω+D_s w)^n≤C(X,ω), D_s=i∂bar∂/π. Nguyen, arXiv:1501.00891v1, Proposition 1.1.
On connected compact Hermitian (X,ω), every genuine ω-psh a with sup_X a=0 satisfies ∫_X|a|ω^n≤C(X,ω). Dinew–Kołodziej, arXiv:0910.3937v1, Proposition 2.1.
passages.quote: there exists a constant C dependent only on X, ω

passages.statement: On compact Hermitian (X,ω), for p>1, nonnegative F∈L^p(ω^n), and compact K⊂X, ∫_K Fω^n≤C(p,X,ω)‖F‖_p cap_ω(K)exp[-a(X,ω)cap_ω(K)^(-1/n)], with positive constants and the ordinary global Hermitian capacity for source operator i∂bar∂/π. No mass-invariance hypothesis is required. Dinew–Kołodziej, Corollary 2.4.

For open Ω⊂R^m, Sh(Ω)∩L^1_loc is closed in L^1_loc and its L^1_loc-bounded subsets are relatively compact. For Ω⊂C^n the analogous assertions hold for Psh(Ω)∩L^1_loc. A distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable canonical psh representative. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, 21 June 2012, Chapter I, Proposition 4.21, Theorem 5.8 and Proposition 5.9.

passages.statement: Locally bounded psh functions v_1,…,v_k on Ω⊂C^n have canonical positive closed mixed products D_B v_1∧…∧D_B v_k, D_B=2i∂bar∂, defined recursively by D_B(v_1D_B v_2∧…∧D_B v_k). These products are symmetric and multilinear and converge weakly under componentwise decreasing limits to locally bounded psh functions. The weighted currents v_0D_B v_1∧…∧D_B v_k also converge under such decreasing limits of all bounded psh factors. For bounded psh u,v and smooth compactly supported test forms, the difference of closed powers equals D_B[(u-v)Σ_(a=0)^(k-1)(D_Bu)^a∧(D_Bv)^(k-1-a)] as a current. Bedford–Taylor, equation (2.1), Theorems 2.1 and 2.4, Corollaries 2.2 and 2.8.

For K compactly contained in Ω⊂C^n and bounded psh v_1,…,v_k on Ω, ∫_K D_Bv_1∧…∧D_Bv_k∧β^(n-k)≤C(K,Ω,n)∏_i‖v_i‖_∞, where β is a fixed Euclidean positive form and D_B=2i∂bar∂. Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.10.

On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex Ω⊂C^n, E⊂Ω is pluripolar exactly when its outer Bedford–Taylor capacity C*(E,Ω) is zero. For Borel E, the inner capacity equals sup_{v∈Psh(Ω),0<v<1}∫_E(D_Bv)^n, D_B=2i∂bar∂, and is bounded by outer capacity. Bedford–Taylor, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 6.9.
passages.quote: is pluripolar if and only if C*(E)=0.

passages.statement: For compact Hermitian (X,ω), the ordinary global capacity cap_ω(E)=sup_{w∈PSH(ω),0≤w≤1}MA_ω(w)(E), with D_s=i∂bar∂/π, satisfies ∫_Eω^n≤C exp[-a cap_ω(E)^(-1/n)] for every Borel E, with positive geometric constants and the value zero at capacity zero. Kołodziej–Nguyen, Proposition 5.1.

On compact Hermitian (X,ω), in the operator convention of Kołodziej–Nguyen’s capacity-dominated-measures paper, let H be continuous positive increasing with ∫_1^∞dx/[xH(x)^(1/n)]<∞, F_H(y)=y/H(y^(-1/n)), and F(X,H) the positive Radon measures satisfying μ(E)≤F_H(cap_ω(E)) for every Borel E. Every nonzero μ∈F(X,H) admits a continuous genuine ω-psh u and finite c>0 with MA_ω(u)=cμ. For continuous genuine ω-psh a,v∈[-1,0] with μ=MA_ω(a)∈F(X,H), sufficiently small I=∫(v-a)_+dμ satisfies sup_X(v-a)≤CΓ(I), with fixed gauge/geometric dependence and Γ(I)→0 as I↓0. Here Γ is the local inverse of t↦t^(n(n+2)+1)κ^(-1)(t^(n+2)), and κ(y)=4C_n[H(y^(-1/n))^(-1/n)+∫_{y^(-1/n)}^∞dx/(xH(x)^(1/n))]. Kołodziej–Nguyen, arXiv:2003.05061v1 and published 2021 article, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 2.5.

For continuous genuine ω-psh a,v∈[-1,0] with μ=MA_ω(a)∈F(X,H), sufficiently small I=∫(v-a)_+dμ satisfies sup_X(v-a)≤CΓ(I), with fixed gauge/geometric dependence and Γ(I)→0 as I↓0. Here Γ is the local inverse of t↦t^(n(n+2)+1)κ^(-1)(t^(n+2)), and κ(y)=4C_n[H(y^(-1/n))^(-1/n)+∫_{y^(-1/n)}^∞dx/(xH(x)^(1/n))]. Kołodziej–Nguyen, arXiv:2003.05061v1 and published 2021 article, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition 2.5.

premises: On a connected compact Hermitian (X,ω), with D_s=i∂bar∂/π, bounded genuine ω-psh a,b,v_1,…,v_(n-1), and T=∧_(i=1)^(n-1)(ω+D_s v_i), satisfy ∫_{a<b}D_s b∧T≤∫_{a<b}D_s a∧T+∫_{a<b}(b-a)D_sT. Kołodziej–Nguyen, arXiv:1312.5491v2, Lemma 2.1.

For a smooth positive Hermitian ω on Ω⊂C^n, 1≤k≤n, and locally bounded genuine ω-psh v_i, the ordinary mixed products ∧_i(ω+D_s v_i), D_s=i∂bar∂/π, converge weakly when each bounded ω-psh sequence decreases pointwise or converges uniformly to v_i. This also holds on compact Hermitian manifolds. Kołodziej–Nguyen, Proposition 1.2.

On compact Hermitian (X,ω), use D_s=i∂bar∂/π and d_s^c=i(bar∂-∂)/(2π). Suppose B>0 satisfies -Bω²≤2nD_sω≤Bω² and -Bω³≤4n²dω∧d_s^cω≤Bω³. For bounded genuine ω-psh a,v, 0<ε<1, m=inf_X[a-(1-ε)v], and U_s={a<(1-ε)v+m+s}, one has ∫_{U_s}(ω+D_s((1-ε)v))^n≤(1+C_nBs/ε^n)∫_{U_s}(ω+D_s a)^n whenever 0<s<ε³/(16B). Kołodziej–Nguyen, Theorem 2.3.

On compact Hermitian (X,ω), with D_s=i∂bar∂/π, cap_ω(E)=sup_{w∈PSH(ω),0≤w≤1}∫_E(ω+D_s w)^n, and B satisfying the torsion bounds -Bω²≤2nD_sω≤Bω² and -Bω³≤4n²dω∧d_s^cω≤Bω³, let bounded genuine ω-psh a≤0 and -1≤v≤0 be given. Set m=inf[a-(1-ε)v], U_s={a<(1-ε)v+m+s}, δ=(1/3)min{ε^n,ε³/(16B)}, δ_0=min{δ,4(1-ε)δ}, 0<ε<1. If H:(0,∞)→(0,∞) is increasing, ∫_1^∞dx/[xH(x)^(1/n)]<∞, and MA_ω(a)(E)≤cap_ω(E)/H(cap_ω(E)^(-1/n)) for every Borel E, then 0<s<δ_0 and 0<cap_ω(U_s)<cap_ω(X) imply s≤κ(cap_ω(U_s)), where κ(y)=4C_n[H(y^(-1/n))^(-1/n)+∫_{y^(-1/n)}^∞dx/(xH(x)^(1/n))]. Independently, 0<s,t≤δ imply [(1-ε)t]^n cap_ω(U_s)≤(1+C_n)MA_ω(a)(U_(s+4(1-ε)t)). Kołodziej–Nguyen, Theorem 5.3 and Lemma 5.4.
On connected compact Hermitian (X,ω), genuine ω-psh a,w with sup_X a=0 and 0≤w≤1 satisfy ∫_X|a|(ω+D_s w)^n≤C(X,ω), D_s=i∂bar∂/π. Nguyen, arXiv:1501.00891v1, Proposition 1.1.
On connected compact Hermitian (X,ω), every genuine ω-psh a with sup_X a=0 satisfies ∫_X|a|ω^n≤C(X,ω). Dinew–Kołodziej, arXiv:0910.3937v1, Proposition 2.1.

On compact Hermitian (X,ω), for p>1, nonnegative F∈L^p(ω^n), and compact K⊂X, ∫_K Fω^n≤C(p,X,ω)‖F‖_p cap_ω(K)exp[-a(X,ω)cap_ω(K)^(-1/n)], with positive constants and the ordinary global Hermitian capacity for source operator i∂bar∂/π. No mass-invariance hypothesis is required. Dinew–Kołodziej, Corollary 2.4.

For open Ω⊂R^m, Sh(Ω)∩L^1_loc is closed in L^1_loc and its L^1_loc-bounded subsets are relatively compact. For Ω⊂C^n the analogous assertions hold for Psh(Ω)∩L^1_loc. A distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable canonical psh representative. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, 21 June 2012, Chapter I, Proposition 4.21, Theorem 5.8 and Proposition 5.9.

Locally bounded psh functions v_1,…,v_k on Ω⊂C^n have canonical positive closed mixed products D_B v_1∧…∧D_B v_k, D_B=2i∂bar∂, defined recursively by D_B(v_1D_B v_2∧…∧D_B v_k). These products are symmetric and multilinear and converge weakly under componentwise decreasing limits to locally bounded psh functions. The weighted currents v_0D_B v_1∧…∧D_B v_k also converge under such decreasing limits of all bounded psh factors. For bounded psh u,v and smooth compactly supported test forms, the difference of closed powers equals D_B[(u-v)Σ_(a=0)^(k-1)(D_Bu)^a∧(D_Bv)^(k-1-a)] as a current. Bedford–Taylor, equation (2.1), Theorems 2.1 and 2.4, Corollaries 2.2 and 2.8.

For K compactly contained in Ω⊂C^n and bounded psh v_1,…,v_k on Ω, ∫_K D_Bv_1∧…∧D_Bv_k∧β^(n-k)≤C(K,Ω,n)∏_i‖v_i‖_∞, where β is a fixed Euclidean positive form and D_B=2i∂bar∂. Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.10.

On a bounded strongly pseudoconvex Ω⊂C^n, E⊂Ω is pluripolar exactly when its outer Bedford–Taylor capacity C*(E,Ω) is zero. For Borel E, the inner capacity equals sup_{v∈Psh(Ω),0<v<1}∫_E(D_Bv)^n, D_B=2i∂bar∂, and is bounded by outer capacity. Bedford–Taylor, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 6.9.
